item.g:title: ʻĀlina: Koʻolau Valley Aerial, Canvas Print, 16 x 20 in
item.g:description: This image was created while on a hike along the Koʻolau Mountain Range. After hiking for hours with my camera gear and drone, I found a launching point in order to gather the 4-6 images which were eventually stitched together to create this image. Over thousands of years the rain and water have carved this incredibly unique and stunning valley with sheer cliffs and deep river beds. Surrounded by lush forest, this is truly a one of a kind scene. Titled ʻĀlina, which means "Scar," this image reminds us that scars can be beautiful.

item.g:title: Kākau: Koko Head Crater Aerial, Canvas Print, 16 x 20 in
item.g:description: This image was created using a drone along the Kaiwi Coast on Oʻahu. A kākau, or "tattoo" common among native Hawaiians. Native Hawaiian body art often include repeating lines, triangles, and other patterns. As I flew the drone over this particular face of Koko Head Crater, I couldn't help but notice the similarities in the landscape to a traditional Hawaiian kākau.

item.g:title: Candlestick: Makapuʻu Lighthouse Sunrise, Canvas Print, 18 x 12 in
item.g:description: This image was created during sunrise using a drone. As I flew along the cliffs of Makapuʻu, I noticed the symmetrical nature of the geography as well as the contrast of light and dark, which combined for an interesting combination. Add in a lighthouse and you get an interesting combination of elements. While editing the image to emphasize the contrast in colors and tone while maintaining a symmetrical composition, I wanted to play off of the idea that there are often two very different sides of the same coin. Makapuʻu lighthouse is perched on the eastern tip of Oʻahu.

item.g:title: Kai Emi: Black Sand Wave Patterns, Canvas Print, 16 x 20 in
item.g:description: The significance of this image is the location is unimportant. On this particular morning, I was having a difficult time discovering new compositions using the rocks along the beach, which are almost always elements in my seascape photography. After trying out a few shots, I did something that I almost never do. I found a black section of the beach and focused on the texture of the sand itself. I broke away from what I knew and tried something different. I was stunned to find that the patterns and textures created by the waves in the sand were absolutely beautiful. My head always told me that there was nothing to be gained from something as uniform and simple as the sand, but if you look close enough, you can always find something interesting.

item.g:description: In a stroke of luck, this image was created in the late morning on the north shore of Oʻahu. As the sun rose behind me, a light drizzle started to fall in the distance revealing a full rainbow. I quickly found an interesting foreground element and photographed this scene. While the image itself obviously arouses feelings of joy, the circumstances of how this was created remind us that we can look up and find reasons to be grateful in every moment.

item.g:title: Kahana: Kahana Bay from the Ridge, Canvas Print, 16 x 20 in
item.g:description: This image was created on the East shore of Oʻahu. Waking up in the early hours of the morning, I hiked up this ridge in complete darkness in order to find this vantage point for sunrise. I am particularly fond of this image because of the sweeping nature of the ridge in the foreground blending seamlessly with the beach below, creating an "S" shape. This image is meant to emphasize the flowing nature of life and how unexpected circumstances can work together to create something beautiful. The valley in view is called Kahana Valley and is one of the more well preserved ahupuaʻa on Oʻahu. An "ahapuaʻa" is a sociological and geological land division from mauka to makai (mountain to sea), which typically held all of the resources for a native Hawaiian community to thrive on.

item.g:title: Mālie: Papailoa Beach, North Shore, Canvas Print, 18 x 12 in
item.g:description: This is easily one of my favorite images I've ever created. Papailoa Beach on the North Shore of Oʻahu has some of the most dynamic scenes. During this particular season, large waves had washed away the sand to reveal a buried reef. The ocean waves cascaded over the sharp edges and gently flowed back and forth. This created a wonderful contrast of sharp rocks and silky water. This echos the proverb that something as fluid as water can overcome the sharpest and immovable rocks.

item.g:description: Literally meaning "two islands" the Mokulua off the shore of Kailua are iconic silhouettes along the horizon. I chose to convert this image to black and white because the light and dark tones were so prominent and telling. By removing the color, you're able to have a greater appreciation for the texture and motion created by the reef and sand.

item.g:title: Pūʻao: Koʻolau Mountains Aerial, Canvas Print, 16 x 20 in
item.g:description: Using a drone and stitching several exposures together, I created this image of a specific section of the Koʻolau Mountain Range on Oʻahu. This specific facade really stood out to me due to its geometrical symmetry combined with the dramatic light from one side. I chose to name this piece Pūʻao, translates to womb. Although typically pointing down, the triangle is often associated as a feminine symbol of strength and fertility. This image of Mother Earth and her fertile body and lush forests show off the miracle that is the female body.

item.g:title: Timespan: Makapuʻu Long Exposure, Canvas Print, 18 x 12 in
item.g:description: I created this image in my early days as a photographer. Hiking along the ridge above Makapuʻu beach during sunrise, I found a stunning vantage point to photograph the coastline leading out to the lighthouse. The sun was coming up just over the cliffs in the distance and the clouds were being blown left to right. This was the perfect opportunity for a long exposure. Totaling 120 seconds, the extended exposure smoothed out the ocean and stretched the clouds to create a time warp effect while maintaining sharpness in the landscape itself.

Only from the air could this pattern be fully appreciated. Pair that with a dramatic cliffside in the distance and it makes for a stunning image. Waimānalo is known for its long sandy beaches, picturesque offshore islets and clear blue waters.
